name: Spanish
blurb: Peninsular Spanish, the Castilian of Spain, taught as a complete system with vosotros in the paradigm from the start and the American forms shown alongside rather than left out. Corlang takes you to B1. Spain asks for A2 plus a civics test for nationality, and this course covers that level thoroughly on the way through, but A2 on its own is a thin place to stop, so B1 is the finish line. The exam it is built around is the DELE, set by the same institution that writes the official syllabus, so the course and the certificate share one map. There is no A0 onramp: Spanish spelling maps onto sound so honestly that you can read aloud from the first lesson, and the five lessons that teach the sound system and the written accent open A1 instead.
paretoSummary: 80% of everyday Spanish comes from a small core. Learn the present tense of the three conjugations and then the four irregular families (querer, poder, pedir, and the yo-form group like hacer and salir), because almost every irregular verb in the language belongs to one of them. Learn ser and estar as a single decision rather than two verbs: what something is against what state it is in. Learn that every noun is masculine or feminine and that the article and every adjective follow it, so agreement is the glue that holds a long sentence together. Learn the object pronouns lo, la, le and the way le turns into se in front of them, because they are the hardest small thing in the language and everything from the imperative to polite requests depends on them. Learn the three past tenses in the order this course teaches them, he hablado for what touches today, hablé for what is closed, hablaba for description and habit, and the moment you can choose between them you can tell a story. Learn the present subjunctive not as a mood to fear but as the form Spanish uses whenever a second clause is wanted, doubted, valued or still to come. And write the accents: hablo and habló are different tenses, and the exam grades that difference. Master this 20% and Spain opens up.
reminderProverb: Poco a poco se anda lejos, a little today is all it takes.
